newsitem.title: USA: Chicago mayor pushes for school funding reform.
newsitem.headline: Chicago mayor pushes for school funding reform.

text.p: Chicago Mayor Richard Daley called Monday for bipartisan action by the Illinois General Assembly on school funding.

In what was termed as the mayor's "year-ahead speech," Daley pointed out that steps have already been taken to reform Chicago's schools and that it was now time to reform the way schools are funded state wide.
He said that property taxpayers have carried the burden of funding schools for too long and that Illinois has ranked near the bottom among states in terms of education funding.
"The state must finally meet its responsibility and must do it in a way that protects taxpayers and is fair to communities throughout the state," Daley said.
The mayor also called on the state to craft a welfare reform plan that protects the quality of life for the elderly, children and people with disabilities, as well as provides job training.
With utility deregulation mulled for Illinois, Daley warned that the wrong plan could hurt rate payers and economic growth.
Crime was also high on the agenda for Daley who said he would unveil this winter a local, regional and national strategy for fighting illegal drugs.

He also pledged to use technology to allow residents to access city government through computers and to continue investments in capital programs, like the $200 million of bond-financed projects slated for Chicago infrastructure and libraries this year.
